headline: OpenAI has published more than 700 AI-written maths papers covering 372 groups of results, and independent mathematicians are still checking how many hold up.
score_reason: Pool score 8 lowered by 1: the release was on 6 Oct, so only the verification status is new today, and the account we could read is a secondary one.
summary: Education Times reports that on 6 Oct 2026 OpenAI released more than 700 research papers, written with an internal AI model, that cover 372 groups of maths results, and that many proofs also come in Lean, a computer language that machine-checks the logic of a proof. Independent mathematicians have not yet accepted the results, some have criticised the papers' quality and clarity, and reports say OpenAI has since withdrawn three papers.
importance_line: Mathematicians and journals now face a flood of AI-written results to check, and it is not yet known how many are correct, so the headline count says little about proven maths.
notes: The pool link (Technology Org, 'what has actually been verified') could not be opened (HTTP 403); this entry rests on the Education Times report of the same story. The withdrawal of three papers is 'according to reports' there and is not independently confirmed here.
